title: One owner, several names, all paid by the City
question: Which City payees with different names belong to one owner, on what evidence, and what was each paid?
finding: 101 owner-groups hold two or more differently named City payees on record evidence (tiers 1 to 4): 41 through the same owner account or ownership name in the City business registry, 10 through a State-numbered licensed person, 48 through a filing that names one as the trade name or related organization of the other (23 of them declared on a tax return) and 2 through an address plus a telephone or named owner. The second and later names in those groups were paid $1.23 billion since fiscal 2019; the largest registry pair is Mckesson Corporation ($567.5 million) and Mckesson Plasma and Biologics LLC ($185.2 million). A further 199 pairs of payees share only a suite-level address (tier 5) or an address and a surname (tier 6) and are leads, not groups.
how: City payee names since fiscal 2019 are matched on a normalised key (legal suffixes, punctuation and "DBA" removed) to the Treasurer’s business registry, the State contractor-licence file, tax-return related-organization schedules and State cannabis licences. Tier 1: two names under one owner account or one ownership name (for a personal ownership name, only accounts that also share an address). Tier 2: one State person number current on both licences. Tier 3: a filing names one as trade name, parent, subsidiary or related organization of the other. Tier 4: same suite-level address and the same telephone or named owner. Groups are built from tiers 1 to 4 only; tiers 5 and 6 never chain and are shown as pairs. An address is used only if no more than 4 owners were ever registered at the suite (or 8 at a building with no suite written), and owners with more than 10 sites are left out. Rows are ordered by tier, then by the amount paid to the second name.
limits: One owner running several businesses is ordinary, and the City may knowingly pay a parent and its subsidiary, a firm under its old and new name after a merger or renaming, or a nonprofit and the housing partnerships it sponsors (the tier 3 rows declared on a tax return are disclosed by the organizations themselves). The question for a reader is narrower: whether two names were treated as two parties where a rule assumes separate parties; that rule should be checked for each row, because none is stated in these files. Names are matched exactly after normalising, so a common name can pick the wrong company and a misspelt one is missed. The registry names an owner, not officers or shareholders. A name that reads as a private individual’s is replaced by a code; that test uses lists of given and family names from the State licence, City payroll and tax-return files and can miss an unusual name. Many tier 5 rows read as a joint venture and one of its own members, a landlord and tenant, or a manager and a building it runs. The telephone, e-mail domain, suite and officer names printed on the City’s contract-approval notices are not read here; the places cross-check (screen contract-notice-shared-identifiers) lists pairs of City payees tied by them that are in no owner-group on this page.
